transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-15
Time: 14:00 PT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Lena Ortiz (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Dr. Maya Chen, Ethan Rogers, Priya Singh, Carlos Mendez

Summary:
High-level POC scoping focused on quality evaluation plan: golden prompts, regression tests, hallucination checks, scoring approach, workload sizing and timeline for a 6-week pilot. Customer emphasized clinical safety and formatting constraints for EHR-facing outputs; security and audit logging required. Redwood to provide benchmark harness and pilot pricing.

Topics:
- Success criteria and guardrails for clinical outputs
- Workload sizing and throughput expectations (p95 latency targets)
- Benchmark design: golden prompts, hallucination detection, format checks
- Scoring methodology and pass/fail thresholds
- Timelines and pilot/go-live gating

Transcript body:
[00:00] Lena: Hey everyone thanks for joining, I'm Lena from Redwood Inference, i'm the AE on this engagement, with me is Ravi our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:04] Maya: good thanks Lena, a little busy but excited to dive in.
[00:07] Ethan: yeah thanks all, we'll keep it focused, couple of exec time constraints.
[00:12] Lena: perfect, goal for today is to lock the quality eval plan for the POC — what we need from you, what we'll deliver, and timelines. Ravi will run through the benchmark approach.
[00:20] Ravi: hi all, quick context, we typically run a 4-6 week pilot: initial ingest and baseline, run benchmarks on hosted and dedicated variants, iterate on prompts and quantization/settings. For this one we should plan for a quality-first evaluation since outputs will go into clinical notes.
[00:34] Carlos: quick q, when you say hosted vs dedicated, what are the differences we'd notice in latency / cost?
[00:39] Ravi: hosted is our managed API, fastest to start, cost-per-token a bit higher. Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools and predictable throughput — you'd see lower variance at scale and ability to isolate data; you'll also get more control over kv cache and batching settings. sorry — k v cache, sometimes the transcription picks that up weirdly.
[00:54] Priya: security question: we need KMS-backed key management, audit logs, and retention controls. Also any SOC2 or ISO attestations?
[01:02] Lena: yes, we'll send the compliance pack — SOC2 Type II and our InfoSec summary. For KMS, Redwood Private and Dedicated both support customer KMS integrations, and we can enable audit logging to your SIEM. We'll include specifics in the docs we send.
[01:18] Maya: back to quality, primary success criteria are: (1) clinical accuracy (no hallucinations that could mislead care), (2) correct structured formatting to our EHR schema (JSON with specific fields), and (3) latency p95 under 700ms for common prompts. If any of these fails, we can't move to pilot.
[01:34] Lena: noted, that's helpful. For hallucination detection we typically run two layers: automated checks vs a golden set and spot human review. We also run regression tests each model change against benchmark prompts.
[01:45] Ethan: can you expand on the golden prompts? what's in that set?
[01:48] Ravi: golden prompts are curated examples that represent your high-value flows — e.g., discharge summary conversion, med list extraction, problem-list summarization. We ask customers to flag 'golden responses' which are the correct output examples we expect. In benchmarking we compare model responses to those golden outputs via a mix of exact-match, normalized field checks, and a weighted semantic similarity score.
[02:10] Carlos: how do you score hallucinations specifically? we need per-case flags that a clinician can audit quickly.
[02:16] Ravi: good Q. We use a combination: entity-level hallucination detection (unexpected diagnoses/medications), factual consistency checks against the input note, and heuristics for hallucinated assertions. For scoring we output a per-response score and a binary hallucination flag if the heuristics exceed thresholds. We'll provide logs that surface the offending tokens/phrases and a link to the source prompt.
[02:35] Maya: also format checks — our EHR requires ICD codes in a particular field and dates in ISO-8601. If format is wrong we can't auto-ingest.
[02:42] Ravi: we include strict format validators in the pipeline: JSON schema validation and regex checks. We also have post-processing steps that can try to normalize, but we recommend the eval treats normalization failures as errors for the golden set.
[02:56] Lena: on scoring approach, Ravi, walk through the scoring rubric you propose.
[03:00] Ravi: sure. For each golden prompt we compute: field-level exact match (weight 40%), semantic similarity on narrative fields using a embeddings+cosine approach (weight 30%), hallucination penalty (weight -20% if flagged), and format/validation penalty (weight -10% if schema fails). Scores aggregate to a 0-100 scale. We'll suggest thresholds: >=90 pass, 75-90 review, <75 fail. We can tune weights based on your priorities.
[03:28] Ethan: those thresholds sound reasonable but we may want higher for certain safety-critical flows — e.g., medication reconciliation needs 95+.
[03:35] Maya: yes agree. We can tier prompts into critical vs non-critical. Critical ones need a higher bar.
[03:40] Carlos: how do you handle regression tests as we iterate models or quantize? we need a CI-like guardrail.
[03:45] Ravi: we run the full golden set and the full regression suite on every model change in the pilot, and produce a regression diff report showing per-prompt deltas. For quantization/optimize runs we test both latency/cost improvements and quality tradeoffs and recommend a sweet spot. We'll capture p95 latency, median latency, tokens/sec, and cost delta in each run.
[04:05] Priya: on timelines, if we hand over data by next Tuesday, when could the pilot start?
[04:10] Lena: target pilot kickoff the week of 2026-09-28. Ravi can onboard the harness and run initial baselines within ~5 business days after receiving samples. So handover by 2026-09-22 is workable.
[04:20] Ravi: timeline detail — week 1: sample ingest, environment setup, golden prompts ingestion; week 2: baseline runs on hosted + dedicated; week 3: iterations with prompts and quantization; week 4: run regression and hallucination sweeps; week 5: customer human review for flagged cases; week 6: finalize recommendations and gating decision. We can compress to 4 weeks if the sample size is smaller and customers prioritize a narrower set of flows.
[04:45] Maya: sample size — we can provide 10k anonymized notes representing common flows and a separate 500-case gold set with annotated expected outputs. Does that work?
[04:54] Ravi: perfect; 500 gold is ideal. For the 10k we'll stratify by flow type and length distribution so the runtime can be tuned — that helps kernel selection and batching profiles.
[05:05] Ethan: any special infra we need? our infra team prefers VPC peering and Strict egress controls.
[05:10] Lena: Redwood Dedicated or Redwood Private can run in your VPC; we'll include network setup docs. For POC we can use Secure Tunnel + mTLS if peering is a blocker.
[05:20] Priya: please confirm log retention for POC (we need logs for 90 days) and how PII is handled in logs.
[05:26] Ravi: logs can be configured to redact PII and we support configurable retention windows; by default we'll not store full text logs without your consent. We'll include these options in the compliance doc.
[05:36] Carlos: about benchmarks, will you share the actual scoring scripts so we can replicate locally?
[05:40] Ravi: yes, we'll push the benchmark harness (python notebook + dockerized runner) and a README. It includes the scoring functions, hallucination heuristics, and format validators. You can run locally or point it at our hosted endpoints.
[05:52] Lena: ok let's cover explicit success criteria recap. Maya?
[05:55] Maya: 1) Critical flows >=95, non-critical >=90 aggregated; 2) No high-confidence hallucinations in critical flows; 3) p95 latency <700ms on chosen deployment (dedicated preferred but we'll test hosted baseline); 4) EHR schema validation success >99% for auto-ingest flows.
[06:16] Lena: great, we'll codify those into the POC success doc. Final questions?
[06:20] Ethan: pricing — can you send a pilot estimate with expected token volumes and dedicated commit rough numbers?
[06:24] Lena: yes will send with dedicated vs hosted and estimated cost deltas.
[06:28] Priya: can you share your SOC2 cert and a sample PCA?
[06:31] Lena: yes, in the compliance pack we send.
[06:34] Ravi: i'll share the benchmark template and a small set of sample golden prompts after the call.
[06:38] Lena: perfect. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the artifacts and schedule the kickoff once we have the sample data.
